absent: Definition and initialization of the operations table, grace snapshot types, and pipe update helper.
First part of writer setup before the shown conditional and polled modes, including allocation and sizing of snapshot arrays.
Layout and lifecycle of torture objects, free lists, reader segments, and global tunables and counters.
Semantics of random sleep, stutter, stop checks, thread priority, lazy work, nodelay flag, slow grace periods, stall deadline, and trace dump helpers.
Numeric values of writer states and reader protection bits, shifts, masks, and maximum extension set.
Full grace period ordering guarantees and callback barrier semantics beyond the test usage shown.

findings.text: Update side offers paired controls to nest expedited grace period requests. One increments a shared nesting counter to request expedition and the other decrements it to release, allowing multiple nested requests to be stacked and unwound by test threads.

Writer thread cycles through conditional snapshot and polled grace period modes in normal, expedited, full sequence and expedited full flavors plus a direct synchronous mode. Each iteration announces a get or start state, sleeps a random short interval, announces a sync or wait state, performs the corresponding wait operation, then advances a reuse pipe. An unrecognized mode triggers a one time warning.

Normal and full polling modes maintain small arrays of older completion observations. While waiting for the newly started poll to complete they repeatedly sample current grace state, replace the first array entry found complete or equal to the fresh sample, warn if no entry matches, and sleep a random interval between probes. Expedited polling variants wait only on the single new poll with random sleeps.

After each grace wait the writer increments a global version counter, sometimes adjusts expedition nesting depth through a cycle that grows then reverses while cross checking global expedited and normal indicators, optionally queues per CPU lazy work when that option is enabled, and then enters a stutter delay that can restore normal scheduling priority.

When a stutter delay actually waited, with no forward callback nodelay, no slow grace periods, no stop request and past a stall deadline, the writer scans torture objects for an empty free list on a non current object. On a hit it freezes tracing, optionally calls a grace thread debug hook, warns with the pipe count and dumps the trace buffer.

Writer loop runs until a stop request, then clears the current pointer to signal the statistics task, unwinds any positive expedition nesting into negative releases, warns if expedition remains active while allowed, alerts if expedition was disabled, cancels and destroys lazy work when enabled, frees poll snapshot arrays, marks a stopping state and reports thread exit.

Fake writer is a low priority thread that exits early with a warning if no update primitives are configured. Otherwise until stop it sleeps random jiffies, rarely invokes a callback barrier when available, else exercises one randomly selected primitive among no op deferred free, expedited sync, four conditional get plus sync flavors, four polled start plus wait flavors with optional interrupt masking around start, and direct sync, then stutters.
Timer driven reclamation callback simply releases the memory of the passed callback structure and does nothing else.

Barrier check ignores timer context identified by negative reader id, increments the calling reader loop counter, then tries to delegate verification by randomly choosing distinct checked and checker readers with online coverage, requiring idle local checker slot observed with acquire ordering plus idle object and checker assignment slots, sampling checked loops, recording indices and attempting installation with relaxed compare exchange with back out on contention.

A reader performs delegated verification only when it has an assigner and observes the assigner ready flag with acquire ordering. It samples the designated checked reader loops, counts an attempt and a failure on sequence regression, poisons the stored check value far forward to detect reuse, clears ready, then releases its own assigner slot and the assigner checker slot with release ordering.

Per reader verification record contains own loop counter, pending checked reader index, sampled loop value at assignment time, pointer to the assigning reader record, and a ready flag. The shared torture object carries a single check pointer used as arbitration for one outstanding assignment.

A per CPU boolean records execution inside a synchronous function handler. Extension mask generation and state validation consult it alongside hard and soft interrupt context to suppress interrupt and bottom half changes and to relax over disabling complaints.

Read state validator is active only when a torture checking option is enabled and never in non maskable interrupt context. It warns on mismatch between recorded interrupt, bottom half, preempt, sched and RCU bits and observed interrupt disabled state, hard interrupt state, soft interrupt and preemption counts and operation provided nesting level, with adjusted masks for kernels without preemptible RCU and for real time handling of bottom half state, and it skips over disabling checks in soft or hard interrupt or handler context.

All extension validation warnings share a common diagnostic identifying the function, a phase label for before during or after transition, the current recorded state value, the bits being added and removed, and the current preemption count.

Reader protection transition acquires new coverage before releasing old coverage. Acquisition order is bottom half disable, RCU bottom half lock, interrupt disable, preemption disable, sched RCU lock, then outer and inner RCU locks with opaque indices packed into state bits. Release order is interrupt enable, preemption enable, sched unlock, bottom half enable, RCU bottom half unlock, inner RCU unlock, outer RCU unlock sometimes under task pi lock, then up read. Transition logs CPU and grace data under combined coverage, delays on mid sequence change, and repacks indices with new bits.

Candidate extension mask starts from global extendable bits intersected with operation supported bits plus both RCU reader bits, then is randomly reduced to either a subset or a single bit. Nested RCU bit is fixed to require the outer RCU bit using old mask context, interrupt preempt and bottom half bits are stripped in hard interrupt or handler context, bottom half bits are preserved from old mask when interrupts become masked, real time kernels forbid bottom half changes from atomic context, and empty result falls back to outer RCU bit.
